old: It began as a farmer's tool for tossing grain into a breeze so the husks would blow away.
Its ancestor root simply meant 'to blow.'
It shares that root with Latin ventus — 'wind' — and with Dutch and German words for a winnowing basket.
clues: This everyday comfort item began as a farmer's basket for tossing grain into the wind, so the light husks blew away and left the clean wheat behind.
Today it names anything with blades or a folding sheet that pushes air to cool you, from a handheld paper one to a spinning ceiling one, much simpler than an air conditioner.
In US baseball slang it took on a second meaning, an enthusiast, so a devoted follower of a team or a pop star shares this name.
